title: New product from PRD: one form in the browser reaches a bound repository and a goal
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-5ef1a0a9010c4bfe872ff9b774068234 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-4a0f706437a042059789be2ebdb98bc0, the scaffold) and child 2 (task-facff1d1e7ce44a6b1101490524890a9, the command). PROOF ROW: it owns the browser form, the Playwright journey, the live GitHub drive and the docs (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the 'New product from PRD' form in the browser - directory (new or empty), PRD file, product name, optional GitHub owner/visibility - dispatching child 2's command and then creating the goal with the PRD through the EXISTING `goal.create_with_source`, after which the existing lane continues unchanged.

THE WHOLE POINT IS THAT THE BROWSER IS ENOUGH. This is the row that makes 'a fresh project cannot be started from the browser alone' false - a README clause measured true on 2026-09-03. The journey must therefore use NO scratchpad script and NO seed for any step the product claims to do itself; a bootstrap driven by a helper script proves nothing about the browser.

REFUSALS ARE OPERATOR WORDS. All four of child 2's codes surface here, and BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE is the interesting one: the local bootstrap SUCCEEDED and the GitHub half did not, so the form must say exactly that rather than reading as a total failure. An operator told 'bootstrap failed' when they have a perfectly good local repository will delete it and start again.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04): goal creation from a PRD already exists (`goal.create_with_source`), and the existing goal-create surface is at apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/live-goal-create.ts (its :91 sentence, 'cannot drive the pre-activation chain', is the kind of honest blocker wording this form should reuse rather than invent). The Playwright specs under tests/e2e/control-room/ already drive a real daemon.
definitionOfDone: A 'New product from PRD' form takes directory, PRD file, product name and OPTIONAL GitHub owner/visibility, and dispatches child 2's command. The GitHub fields are visibly optional - a form that implies GitHub is required would hide the local-only path that child 2 exists to support.

A Playwright journey against a REAL daemon completes the whole thing from the browser: directory created, first commit exists (`git log --oneline` = exactly 1 line), repository bound, project in the manager catalog, PRD goal created and the lane continuing. `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted. NO scratchpad script and NO seed is used for any step - this row's claim is that the BROWSER is sufficient, and a helper script anywhere in the path voids it.

The four refusals render as operator words with their codes VERBATIM, and BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE renders as a PARTIAL success: the local repository exists and is bound, only the GitHub half did not. Assert that wording specifically - 'bootstrap failed' here would make an operator delete a good repository.

LIVE DRIVE: a throwaway repository created under the owner's GitHub account from the browser - URL and receipt id in a row comment under ~4500 chars. The owner's account and visibility are supplied by the owner, never invented. If `gh` is absent or unauthenticated on the lane, record the BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE refusal verbatim together with the successful LOCAL bootstrap - that is a complete outcome, not a partial one.

README's 'a fresh project cannot be started from the browser alone' clause and the VISION Stage 2 'repository bootstrapping' / 'new repository creation' status lines are rewritten to the measured truth, WITH the date of the live drive. `git grep -n 'cannot be started from the browser alone'` returns 0 hits.
Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: NO SCRIPT, NO SEED, ANYWHERE IN THE JOURNEY. The claim is that the browser alone is sufficient; a scratchpad helper in the path makes the claim false while the test stays green.
A PARTIAL SUCCESS IS RENDERED AS ONE. BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE means the local repository is fine - say so, or an operator destroys good work.
THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD: a scaffold defect is child 1's, a command defect is child 2's. Comment there and report_blocked.
THE OWNER'S GITHUB ACCOUNT AND VISIBILITY ARE THE OWNER'S. Never invent an owner, never make a repository public by default, and never let a credential reach the form or a log.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check any new testid namespace is free; keep every production file under 250 lines.

implementationPlan.description:
THE LIVE WIRING. NEW `apps/control-room/src/v2/products/live-new-product.tsx` — the module that talks to the daemon, kept apart from the form so each stays under 250 lines.

IT DOES TWO THINGS:
(1) DISPATCHES `repository.bootstrap` with the operator's real typed values — `{dir, productName, profileVersion}` plus, ONLY when the operator asked for it, `{github: {owner, name, visibility}}`. **Do NOT route this through `DEV_PAYLOADS`**: worker-7bdbffac censused that roster and it needs no edit, because this form sends real values, not a dev payload. `live-dispatch-payloads.ts` is not this row's file.
(2) READS THE RECEIPT BACK from `POST /repository/bootstrap/read` — the route task-53267f86 landed and this row is on record as the consumer for. Decode it with an EXACT-KEY decoder over the closed eight keys, in the style the other `live/` readers use. **THIS IS THE CONSUMER EDGE that retires the census entry in step 7**; without a real call site the route stays advertised and unconsumed.

THE OUTCOME IS CLASSIFIED HERE, NOT IN THE FORM, and there are FOUR states, not two:
  - `outcome: "BOOTSTRAPPED"`, `githubRefusal: null` -> FULL SUCCESS;
  - `outcome: "BOOTSTRAPPED"`, `githubRefusal` non-null -> **PARTIAL SUCCESS**, carrying the code (`BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE`) and its detail. The local repository is REAL, COMMITTED AND BOUND;
  - `outcome: "REFUSED"` -> a hard refusal, carrying `refusal.code` and `refusal.refusedBy`;
  - no receipt -> nothing was attempted, which is not the same as a refusal.
Carry the CODE VERBATIM out of this module. Never derive an outcome from the absence of `remoteUrl` — inferring the refusal from a missing remote is the invented authority the prerequisite row exists to make unnecessary (risk B).

AFTER A SUCCESSFUL BOOTSTRAP, create the goal with the PRD through the EXISTING `goal.create_with_source`. Do not reimplement goal creation and do NOT grow `live-goal-create.ts` — it is 275 lines, already past the 250 target, and this row reads it rather than owning it.

NO CREDENTIAL REACHES THIS MODULE, its state, or any log line (risk C).

(1) DISPATCH. `bootstrapPayload()` sends the operator's real typed values `{dir, productName, profileVersion}` and OMITS `github` entirely when it was not asked for - not an empty object, which would ask the daemon for a repository named nothing. FOUR STATES, CLASSIFIED IN THE READER, NOT THE FORM. `classifyReceipt()` reads the daemon's own `outcome` and `githubRefusal` and nothing else: BOOTSTRAPPED + null githubRefusal = FULL_SUCCESS; BOOTSTRAPPED + non-null = PARTIAL_SUCCESS carrying the code and detail verbatim; REFUSED = REFUSED carrying refusal.code/detail/refusedBy; absent or undecodable = NO_RECEIPT with its own code, which is not a refusal. `remoteUrl` is never consulted to decide anything (risk B).

A MEASURED GAP IN STEP 2'S OWN INSTRUCTION, HANDLED BY REUSE RATHER THAN A BLOCK. The step says to create the goal through `goal.create_with_source` after a successful bootstrap. A PARTIAL success CONTINUES to the goal: the local repository is real, committed and bound.

THE FORM LANDED. apps/control-room/src/v2/products/new-product-form.tsx, 246 lines, presentation only, no authority of its own.

FOUR INPUTS, testids in the cr.newproduct namespace claimed in step 1(d): cr.newproduct.dir (directory, new or empty), cr.newproduct.name (product name), cr.newproduct.prd (PRD file), cr.newproduct.github.owner / .name / .visibility.

THE GITHUB FIELDS ARE VISIBLY OPTIONAL, IN THE LABEL (DoD 1). The fieldset legend reads "GitHub repository (optional) - leave the owner blank to stay local only", the owner label reads "GitHub owner (optional)" and its placeholder reads "Blank means no GitHub repository is requested". Not a tooltip. The caption at cr.newproduct.github.note adds "Nothing is sent to GitHub unless you type an owner." The form submits with every GitHub field empty, and `submit()` then passes NO `github` key at all - `...(github === undefined ? {} : { github })` - so the key is ABSENT, not empty, and the local-only path is reachable.

VISIBILITY CANNOT DEFAULT TO PUBLIC. `DEFAULT_VISIBILITY = "private"` is an exported named constant so a test can assert it directly, and VISIBILITY_OPTIONS lists private, internal, public in that order with private first. The owner is only ever what the operator typed; nothing here invents one (task rail 4).

FOUR OUTCOMES AS OPERATOR WORDS WITH THE CODES VERBATIM (DoD 3), in the exported pure function `newProductWords(run)` so the wording is testable without mounting:
- SUCCESS: "Product created." plus the dir, the sha and the remote when there is one.
- PARTIAL: "Product created here. GitHub was not reached." then "The repository at <dir> exists, is committed at <sha> and is bound to this project. Keep it. Only the GitHub half did not happen: the daemon reported BOOTSTRAP_GH_UNAVAILABLE (<detail>). You can add a remote later; nothing local needs redoing." The word "failed" appears nowhere on this branch and the sentence that would make an operator delete the repository is replaced by an explicit instruction to keep it. The code is shown ALONGSIDE the words, never instead of them.
- ERROR (hard refusal): "The product was not created." then "<code> (<detail>) refused by <refusedBy>." A detail ending in _LOCAL_REPOSITORY_RETAINED (BOOTSTRAP_BIND_FAILED, BOOTSTRAP_CATALOG_FAILED) is NOT reported as "No repository was created" - the daemon says the local repository was retained, so the form says it was created, is still on disk and is not bound yet. Reporting those two as total failures would be the same harm as mis-rendering the GitHub half.
- UNKNOWN (no receipt): "No bootstrap receipt was read." plus the read code at its layer, said plainly to be not a refusal, and a warning that a blind retry over an already-set-up directory is refused BOOTSTRAP_DIR_NOT_EMPTY.
A dispatch-level refusal (no receipt was even attempted) is its own branch and says so rather than claiming a repository state it cannot see.

NO CREDENTIAL FIELD, no token input, no session value in any rendered string. `grep -niE "credential|token|password|secret"` over the file returns only the two docblock lines that say there is none.

RAIL 5: ASCII-only (`LC_ALL=C grep -n '[^ -~\t]'` = 0 hits) and ZERO apostrophes anywhere in the file, JSX text or otherwise (`grep -n "'"` = 0 hits), so the scheduler package-boundary scan has nothing to catch.
